welcome.title: Welcome to {{app}}
welcome.content:
{{app}} keeps your notes, your snippets and your lists within reach of a shortcut.

- Cards file themselves: pinned, today, this week, older.
- The square chip on a card says which folder it lives in. Try the "Board" view at the top: folders are regions there, and notes are dropped into them with the mouse.
- Everything is local: the database lives in your user folder, nothing goes over the network.

These four notes are samples. Edit them, or send them to the trash: the "About → Getting started" menu tells the same story and does not go away.

security.title: Security
security.note: It opens the library at every launch. Changing it re-encrypts nothing: your notes stay sealed with the same key, which is why it takes a second rather than a rewrite.
security.dialogLead: The new one applies at the next launch. This session carries on as it is.
security.changed: Passphrase changed. The old one no longer opens the library, nor the copies kept beside it.
security.backupsNote: At most one copy a day, the last three kept beside the library — enough for an emptied trash or an update gone wrong. Not a defence against a dead disk: export somewhere else for that.
security.changedOneLeft: Passphrase changed, but one copy could not be rewrapped: it still opens with the old phrase.
security.changedSomeLeft: Passphrase changed, but {{count}} copies could not be rewrapped: they still open with the old phrase.
security.copiesNote: The copies kept beside the library are rewrapped with it. A key file you copied somewhere else will still open with the old phrase.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.subtitle: What {{app}} can do, in the order you meet it.
gettingStarted.hint: The sample notes from the first launch show all of this for real.

notes.title: Notes and snippets
notes.body: A note carries a title, a body coloured according to its language, a source and tags. Click a card to open it, or copy its content without opening it from the card's button. Nothing is saved while a note is empty: a note opened and then abandoned leaves no trace.

spaces.title: Spaces to file things in
spaces.body: Every note lives in a space — "Personal", "Work", whatever you like. The switcher at the top left filters the canvas, and "All spaces" shows them together. Deleting a space always asks where its notes should go: they never disappear with it.

folders.title: Folders, and a board
folders.body:
A space stays one pile ordered by date, which answers "what was I doing yesterday" very well and "where do I keep my SQL about indexing" not at all. A folder cuts a space into named, coloured regions: the square chip on a card says where it lives, and a card with no chip is filed nowhere — which is a perfectly good state to be in.

The "Date / Board" switch opens the second view of the same space. A zone moves by its grip, resizes from its corner, and is drawn with the mouse on the empty background. Dragging a note into a zone files it; dropping it on the background takes it out. Moving a zone carries its notes, resizing one catches none. Without a mouse: {{check}} to tick cards, then "File into" in the selection bar.

Clicking a zone's title goes inside it: an ordinary grid, a search that does not leave the folder, and a note created there arrives already filed. Deleting a folder never deletes its notes — they simply become loose again.

organise.title: Finding things: search, tags, filters
organise.body: The search runs through titles, bodies, sources and checklist items, accents included. The left rail filters by tag and by language, and the quick filters isolate the pinned ones or those carrying a deadline. Sorting, grouping by date and the sections are computed by the engine, not by the interface.

fields.title: Fields to fill in
fields.body: Write a field between double braces in a snippet — a name alone, or a name and a default value — and {{app}} asks you for it when you copy. What you type is kept with the note, and global variables (File → Preferences → Variables) propose a value for the whole corpus, shown in grey until you replace it.

checklists.title: Lists to tick
checklists.body: A note is either a snippet or a todo list: an ordered run of items, tickable from the card without opening it. In the editor, Enter adds an item, and Alt with an arrow — or a pointer drag — moves it within the list.

palette.title: Pasting without leaving what you are doing
palette.body: {{palette}} opens the quick-paste palette over any application: type, choose, and the content lands in the clipboard. {{capture}} does the opposite and files the clipboard into a fresh note, {{newNote}} opens an empty one. All three work with the window closed, {{app}} staying in the system tray.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.body: Drop a file on the window while a note is open, or paste an image from the clipboard: it is copied next to the database and attached to the note. The card shows the count, and a preview grows on click.

trash.title: A trash, and Ctrl+Z
trash.body: Deleting a note sends it to the trash, where it stays thirty days before going for good. The banner that follows a deletion offers to take it back, and Ctrl+Z still does after the banner is gone. The trash opens from the quick filters.

transfer.title: In and out
transfer.body: The File menu exports everything, one space or the selection into a file {{app}} can read back, and imports without ever creating a duplicate. "Copy as Markdown" puts the selection in the clipboard, ready to paste into a ticket or a message.

vault.createLead: Choose a passphrase. {{app}} will ask for it once at every launch.
vault.noRecovery: ⚠️ This passphrase cannot be recovered. Lose it and the library goes with it — a plaintext export is the only copy that does not depend on it.
vault.unlockLead: Enter your passphrase to open your notes.
vault.damagedLead: SQLite refuses to read {{app}}'s database. A passphrase will not help — the file itself is broken, and writing to it now would make it worse.
vault.damagedAction: Set it aside and start fresh
vault.damagedNote: ⚠️ The damaged database and its attachments are moved into a folder of their own, and what can still be read is rescued beside them. Your passphrase does not change. {{app}} then opens on an empty library.
vault.setAside: Library set aside in {{path}}. Enter your passphrase to start on a fresh one.
